title: Separating qIND and gqIND for Classical Encryption
summary: For classical symmetric-key encryption, gqIND security implies qIND security, while whether the converse fails for any scheme remains open.

formal_statement.body: For classical symmetric-key encryption schemes, $\mathrm{gqIND}$ security implies $\mathrm{qIND}$ security, but it is unknown whether the two notions can be separated. Construct a classical symmetric-key encryption scheme that is $\mathrm{qIND}$-secure but not $\mathrm{gqIND}$-secure, or prove that no such scheme exists.

scope.domain: This concerns quantum indistinguishability notions for classical symmetric-key encryption schemes.
scope.unresolved_remainder: Determine whether qIND and gqIND can be separated by constructing a qIND-secure but not gqIND-secure classical symmetric-key encryption scheme, or prove that none exists.

citations.label: Semantic Security and Indistinguishability in the Quantum World

progress.summary: The source states the established implication from gqIND security to qIND security and explicitly leaves their separation within classical encryption schemes as an open question.
citation_labels: Tommaso Gagliardoni et al., Semantic Security and Indistinguishability in the Quantum World
